$comment: The pass bar for the agent edit-format probe (myne-md/myne#529, task 5).
The numbers live here rather than in core/src/plugins/agent/probe.rs so there
is one place to find them and one place that can carry the measurements that
produced them. The desktop plugin include_str!s this file, so there is no
second copy to drift.
STATUS: UNMEASURED, and what that does and does not mean is worth stating
precisely, because an earlier version of this comment overstated it.
What IS measured, on every call: the probe itself. It hands the backend one
note and asks for one anchored edit, then runs the real placer over the real
reply. A backend that cannot produce a placeable edit fails that, today, with
no calibration involved. The question the probe asks is not provisional.
What is NOT measured: the cut point. `attempts` and `required` below are a
guess at how many tries a usable backend should need, and nobody has run the
probe against a real model on real hardware, so `measurements` is empty and
stays empty rather than being filled with numbers nobody took.
Why that is shippable rather than a blocking obligation, which is what this
comment used to call it. Three things carry it. The gate is a behavioural
test either way, per the paragraph above. The surface behind it is off by
default: agent mode needs the `ai_enabled` runtime beta opt-in, so nobody
meets this cut point without asking for the feature. And the refusal SAYS SO:
`ProbeThreshold::provisional` is carried to the frontend and rendered as
`agent.composer.unsupportedProvisional` beside the counts, so a user told
their model cannot make precise edits also reads that the bar is provisional.
Telling someone their model is unsuitable is a claim, and a claim resting on
an unmeasured cut point should say so where it is made rather than only here.
The cost of the guess is bounded and runs both ways: too lax offers the
feature on a backend that will produce edits the host then refuses, which
burns requests and, on the remote arm, money; too strict hides the feature
from a backend that works. Neither loses data, and neither is silent.
How to measure, so this stops being a guess: run the probe against at least
three backends spanning the range (a small quantized local model, a mid-size
local model, a remote provider), 20 attempts each, and record pass counts in
`measurements`. Then set `attempts` and `required` so that a backend a user
would call usable passes and one that fails most attempts does not, and flip
`status` to `measured`. `probe_threshold()` asserts the two agree, so a
`measured` status with an empty `measurements` fails the build.
